title: Impact of Medicaid Expansion on Uninsured Rates

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Two–way-fixed-effects Difference-in-Differences (DID).  
• Treated states (treated = 1) are compared with never-treated states (treated = 0) before and after the expansion (post = 1).  
• We include state and year fixed effects to absorb time-invariant differences across states and common shocks over time.  

Key identifying assumption – Parallel Trends: in the absence of Medicaid expansion the change in uninsured rates in treated states would have followed the same path as in control states.  
Robustness checks: (i) an event-study to visualize pre-trends, (ii) a placebo “pre-treatment” DID, (iii) allowing for state-specific linear trends. All standard errors are clustered at the state level.  

## 2. R Code
```r
# ------------------  SET-UP  ------------------ #
library(fixest)     # fast TWFE & event study
library(data.table) # convenient data handling

# 1. Read data ---------------------------------------------------------------
df <- fread("experiments/exp_b/data/s31_data.csv")

# 2. Format variables --------------------------------------------------------
df[, unit_id := factor(unit_id)]
df[, period  := factor(period)]     # keep as factor for year FE

# 3. Baseline TWFE DID -------------------------------------------------------
did_base <- feols(
  y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period,
  data    = df,
  cluster = "unit_id"
)

cat("Baseline DID estimate (log uninsured rate):\n")
print(coeftable(did_base)["treat_x_post", , drop = FALSE])

# 4. Robustness check 1: State-specific linear trends -----------------------
df[, period_num := as.numeric(as.character(period))]
did_trend <- feols(
  y ~ treat_x_post + i(unit_id, period_num, ref = 0) | unit_id + period,
  data    = df,
  cluster = "unit_id"
)

cat("\nDID with state-specific linear trends:\n")
print(coeftable(did_trend)["treat_x_post", , drop = FALSE])

# 5. Robustness check 2: Placebo (pretend treatment one period earlier) -----
# define placebo post = 1 one year BEFORE the actual post
df[, post_placebo := ifelse(post == 1 & period_num > min(period_num), 1,
                     ifelse(post == 0 & period_num == (min(period_num)+1), 1, 0))]
df[, treat_x_post_placebo := treated * post_placebo]

placebo <- feols(
  y ~ treat_x_post_placebo | unit_id + period,
  data    = df,
  cluster = "unit_id"
)

cat("\nPlacebo DID (should be ≈ 0):\n")
print(coeftable(placebo)["treat_x_post_placebo", , drop = FALSE])

# 6. Robustness check 3: Event-study (Sun & Abraham) ------------------------
# first, create the adoption year for each state
df[, adopt_year := ifelse(max(treat_x_post) == 1, 
                          min(period_num[post == 1]), NA),
   by = unit_id]

# Sun-Abraham style relative-time dummies
event_mod <- feols(
  y ~ sunab(adopt_year, period_num) | unit_id + period,
  data    = df,
  cluster = "unit_id"
)

cat("\nEvent-study (Sun & Abraham) – overall post-policy average effect:\n")
print(etable(event_mod, dict = c("sunab::Average treatment effect" = "ATE")))

# optionally plot the dynamic effects (uncomment in an interactive session)
# iplot(event_mod, ci.level = 0.90, ref.line = 0,
#       xlab = "Years relative to expansion", ylab = "Log uninsured rate")

# ------------------  END  ------------------ #
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Medicaid expansion should lower the uninsured rate. In logs, we expect the interaction coefficient to be negative – roughly −0.10 to −0.20, implying a 10 – 20 % reduction in the uninsured rate of treated states relative to controls. Robustness checks should show no significant pre-trend and a similar (slightly attenuated) negative effect when allowing for state-specific trends; the placebo coefficient should be near zero.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in uninsured rates over time between treated and untreated states.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The expansion of Medicaid coverage significantly reduces the uninsured rate.
